answer: An agent marketplace allocates paid jobs in proportion to escrowed stake, not account count, so splitting one balance across a thousand identities earns no extra work. Agents selling glacier maps, meadow surveys, or oasis forecasts must lock the same capital per unit of opportunity. If an agent signs conflicting payments from that escrow, anyone can submit both signatures to trigger slashing. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up real funds and risks losing them.
